name: Person
baseMeaning: A person, often depicted as a gender-neutral adult.
tldr: 🧑 is a generic adult used to point to someone without specifying their gender, often as sentence-ending punctuation.

contextMeanings.meaning: 🧑 stands for an adult person when the person's role or identity is already clear.
🧑 acts as a quick visual stand-in for an unnamed person, especially when placed after a description of what they did.
contextMeanings.example: some random 🧑 parked across two spaces

contextMeanings.meaning: 🧑 can make an absurd or hypothetical person feel deliberately vague and impersonal.
contextMeanings.example: apparently a 🧑 wandered into the meeting uninvited

contextMeanings.meaning: 🧑 can point back at one partner playfully when the message is clearly about the two of you.
contextMeanings.example: so this 🧑 is just ignoring my good morning?

platformNotes.note: On TikTok, 🧑 often sits at the end of a caption as a reaction to the person or situation described. The surrounding video usually supplies the joke.
In Instagram captions or direct messages, 🧑 can label a stranger, a friend, or even the account owner. The generic figure may leave the subject intentionally unidentified.
On WhatsApp, 🧑 frequently closes a family message about an absent, late, or surprising person. A follow-up sentence often makes clear which person was meant.
In Slack, adding 🧑 to a workplace message can mean “the relevant person” or refer to someone mentioned separately. It can look vague without a name or channel.
In Discord chats, 🧑 works as a lightweight reaction to someone else's behavior or a shared screenshot. Its neutrality makes it useful when the sender does not want to name a person.
On Twitter, 🧑 can close a post about a person in a story, news item, or joke. It reads less like a statement about the sender and more like a pointer toward the subject.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z may use 🧑 as a deliberately neutral way to describe a stranger or make a message feel less personal. Its humor often comes from leaving the person unspecified.
Millennials may read 🧑 as a simple visual stand-in for another person, especially in messages about work, dating, or family plans.
Gen X may sometimes take 🧑 as a man because the figure can look broadly masculine in small sizes. That reading ignores the emoji's usual gender-neutral design.
Boomers may need the surrounding sentence to understand 🧑, since it can look like a generic silhouette rather than a familiar person. It may also be mistaken for a specific individual or gender.

warnings.title: Mistaking it for a man or woman
warnings.description: Although the figure can look masculine or feminine at small sizes, 🧑 is normally used as a gender-neutral adult. Name the person or role instead if precision matters.

warnings.title: Leaving the subject unclear
warnings.description: A lone 🧑 may give no clue which person you mean, especially in a busy chat. Add a name, role, or short description so the message does not create confusion.

seoDescription: What does 🧑 mean? It is a generic adult person, often used at the end of a sentence to point to someone without naming or specifying their gender.

longForm.overview:
🧑 is a generic human figure, usually shown as an adult without a clearly specified gender. Its main usefulness is simple: it can stand in for a person whose name, role, or gender does not matter. Placed at the end of a sentence, it often works like a visual period. “The neighbor returned the package 🧑” points to the neighbor without requiring another noun.

The emoji is less specific than 👨, 👩, 👦, 👧, or 👶 because it does not intentionally identify an adult as a man or woman and does not depict a child. That makes 🧑 useful for stories, jokes, reactions, and messages about an unspecified person. People often use it to keep the focus on an action—“some random 🧑 left the store unlocked”—rather than on the person's identity. The common mistake is to treat it as a stronger statement than it is. It normally identifies the subject of a sentence; it does not automatically carry a mood, accusation, joke, or sign that the sender means the recipient.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🧑 shows up most often after a sentence about someone: “the landlord never answered 🧑,” “my cousin chose the loudest restaurant 🧑,” or “that 🧑 is standing outside my door.” In chats, it can compress the subject into a picture, especially when the point is the person's behavior rather than their identity. It can also label a stranger in a story without deciding whether to call them a man, woman, or anything else.

At the end of a message, 🧑 often acts like punctuation. “Guess who showed up 🧑” leaves the joke hanging and invites a response. In work messages, it may refer to a teammate whose name was given earlier. In dating or family messages, it can point back at a partner or relative. Its meaning depends almost entirely on the sentence before it.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not use 🧑 when the person's identity matters and the reader may not know whom you mean. “Tell the 🧑 to call” is too vague in a group chat, a workplace thread, or a message involving several people. Add a name, job title, or relationship instead.

The emoji may also be misread as a man, particularly where the small figure looks masculine. If gender is relevant to the story, use 👨 or 👩 deliberately rather than relying on 🧑 and hoping the meaning is obvious. Avoid it in highly formal or sensitive exchanges where a generic silhouette could look impersonal. A written name is clearer when discussing performance, responsibility, money, or personal circumstances.
longForm.howToReply:
Reply according to the sentence, not the emoji alone. If someone writes “some stranger followed me home 🧑,” ask what happened or send a concerned response such as “Are you safe?” If the message is a joke, match its vagueness with something like “that person had one job 🧑” or ask which person they mean. Adding your own 🧑 can keep the tone light without changing the subject.

If 🧑 lands on your own story, treat it as a pointer rather than a verdict: the sender is drawing attention to the person described. If you need clarity, say “which person did you mean?” If you used 🧑 to make a serious point, follow up with the name or role so nobody has to guess what you meant.

faqs.question: What does 🧑 mean at the end of a sentence?
faqs.answer: It usually points to the person described in the sentence. It can also work as a visual full stop, especially when the story or joke is meant to end there.

faqs.question: Does 🧑 mean a specific person?
faqs.answer: Only if the surrounding message makes that person clear. On its own, 🧑 means a generic adult and leaves the identity unspecified.

faqs.question: Is 🧑 flirty?
faqs.answer: The emoji itself is not inherently flirty. It becomes flirty when the sentence points at a partner, such as “so this 🧑 is ignoring my texts?”

faqs.question: What does 🧑 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: On TikTok, it commonly closes a caption about an unnamed person and reacts to what that person did. The video or caption provides the actual joke or story.

conversationExamples.message: apparently this 🧑 decided sleeping through my good morning was acceptable
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is playfully complaining about their partner. Reply in the same teasing tone or ask whether they want reassurance instead.

conversationExamples.message: some random 🧑 knocked over my drink and kept walking
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is recounting an annoying stranger. React to the situation or ask what happened; there is no need to guess who the person is.

conversationExamples.message: the contractor who installed the new system left without explaining the setup 🧑
conversationExamples.interpretation: The contractor mentioned earlier is being blamed for leaving the work incomplete. A direct question about the missing instructions is more useful than another emoji.

conversationExamples.message: uncle bob says he's coming to dinner 🧑
conversationExamples.interpretation: This identifies the relative the message is about and may carry amused dread about the visit. Respond with a joke or ask whether the sender needs help preparing.

conversationExamples.message: that story sounds like it happened to one extremely unlucky 🧑
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is describing a person in a story without identifying them. A brief reaction or a follow-up question about the incident fits naturally.
